affiliateAudit.observedProduction: 167 Meta-labelled /go requests: 128 webindexer and 39 externalagent, all HTTP204. One unlabelled HTTP307. No evidence that these observed Meta requests inserted outbound clicks.
affiliateAudit.why204: isCrawlerUserAgent lowercases the UA and matches crawler inside the reference URL /webmasters/crawler or /web-crawlers. The guard returns before awaiting parameters, creating the data source, offer/product reads, INSERT or redirect.
affiliateAudit.reproducedGap: Official short meta-webindexer/1.1, meta-externalagent/1.1 and meta-externalfetcher/1.1 do not contain any old pattern. Actual released route with existing isolated test fixtures performs two reads, inserts one unknown click and returns the affiliate HTTP307 for each.
affiliateAudit.fix: Add only the three documented names to the existing CRAWLER_USER_AGENT_PATTERNS. No replacement guard, classifier, route or tracking mechanism.
affiliateAudit.semantics: Recognized bots remain 204/X-Robots-Tag:noindex,nofollow,noarchive with zero data-source calls. Browser and Facebook in-app navigation retain original destination/source/likely_human semantics. Missing UA still redirects and is classified likely_automated; unusual clients remain unknown. Existing invalid identity, unavailable stock, unsafe destination and read-error behavior is unchanged.

cpuFindings: All target pages are dynamically rendered. Production HTML cache-control is private/no-cache/no-store. A successful lifecycle data cache hit does not cache the complete HTML or Flight response.

Product metadata and body issue two different product SELECT projections. Body reads offers, exact variants/proofs, retailer bindings and history; better-value alternatives separately loads and normalizes the category/format pool. There is no database call for every offer. Queries and this behavior are unchanged.

Compare/category hubs already cache successful data for an hour with synchronous bucket rollover and fail-closed errors. React.cache is request memoization. Warm data avoids the catalogue read; server rendering, control/selector creation and client-prop serialization still run.

On a compare data miss, products paginate in batches of 200 with exact-count/completeness guards, retailer-product variant reads, per-variant selection normalization and approved-fact enrichment. Selected pairs read only their offer history. PR #562 proof optimization remains in place.

Source and instrumentation confirm repeated new Intl.NumberFormat for each GBP amount and new Intl.DateTimeFormat for each shared check badge. Warm creatine fixture: 238 NumberFormat and 95 DateTimeFormat constructions per render, reduced to 0 and 4. Warm pre-workout: 260/152 reduced to 0/1. The remaining constructors are in unchanged helpers.

Twelve additional /compare.rsc requests have public request_path=/compare and no bot label. Together with 71 HTML requests they match 83 compare function invocations. This does not prove that those twelve are Meta requests or prefetches.
Existing selector choice/clear links disable prefetch; retailer links are native anchors. Other product navigation can use Next Link. No prefetch behavior is changed.

An empty warm /compare uses neither optimized formatter in the fixture; it is a negative control. The patch does not establish a meaningful improvement for that route. Full Next Flight encoding, DB execution/network and production request composition remain unprofiled.

changes: Reuse the existing native GBP formatter object; keep identical locale and options.
Reuse the existing native Europe/London date formatter object; format the supplied timestamp on every call.
Recognize documented bare Meta crawler names in the existing outbound guard.
implementation.notADataCache: Only stateless Intl configuration objects persist. No formatted amounts, timestamps, offers, stock or nutrition results are retained. No new Data Cache, TTL, invalidation, table, query, dependency, endpoint or service.

localBenchmark.scope: Offline actual page/data modules and React production static SSR; synthetic fixtures, no production/network/SQL execution or full Next HTTP/Flight encoding. Only framework hooks/links/images and chart DOM are substituted. Entire HTML, metadata, client-boundary props and read shapes must match. Existing hour-bucket hub cache is simulated separately from request memoization; cold means hub-data miss, not a Vercel cold start. Revisions use separate processes, one timed at a time; formatter counters run separately from uninstrumented timings.
localBenchmark.interpretation: Local CPU timings only, not observed Vercel savings. Complete HTML, metadata, client-boundary props and read-shape parity are required. Initial query rows/bytes and warm/cold-hub query counts are unchanged.
localBenchmark.exploration: Earlier shared-heap and development-mode runs were noisy, including an apparent product slowdown and nonzero differences in the no-formatter control. Final reported data use separate production-mode processes, alternating batches and a negative control. No conclusion is drawn from the exploratory runs; their files remain in ignored tmp/meta-cpu-audit.

metaRoles.webindexer: Indexes content for Meta AI search and citations.
metaRoles.externalagent: Crawls for model training and direct product/content indexing.
metaRoles.externalfetcher: Fetches individual links at a user request; may ignore robots.txt.
metaRoles.facebookexternalhit: Fetches shared-link previews for Facebook, Instagram and Messenger; some security checks may ignore robots.txt.
metaRoles.identity: UA strings and Vercel bot labels do not independently verify sender identity. Unknown labels do not prove human traffic.

policyProposals.recommendation: Prefer measured code-only reduction first. No blanket Meta, product/category or canonical /compare block.

options.scope: Optional existing-WAF deny on /go/* only, UA contains meta-webindexer or meta-externalagent.
options.benefit: At most the current all-/go function total 1.79 CPU seconds per 30 minutes; exact Meta-only CPU is unavailable. CDN/WAF request costs remain. Existing app already does zero downstream work for observed agents.
options.risk: Changes their /go status from 204 to 403; UA is spoofable. Product/category discovery remains open. Do not extend to browsers, Google/Bing, facebookexternalhit or user-initiated externalfetcher.
options.rollback: Disable only the newly approved rule and confirm existing 204 early-return behavior; verify human 307 in isolated tests or existing legitimate traffic. No database rollback.

options.scope: Only if a separate audit proves waste: exact /compare with left/right query parameters and the two indexer/agent UA families; keep clean /compare, product/category routes, social preview and user-initiated fetchers available.
options.benefit: Unknown matching share of 5.96 total compare CPU seconds per 30 minutes. Current API readback does not establish query-parameter distribution, so do not claim that whole saving or apply a threshold.
options.risk: Parameterized comparisons are noindex,follow but may still help Meta AI answer a specific comparison. Clean /compare is indexable. Do not block the canonical route, all RSC or all Meta traffic.
options.rollback: Disable only the reviewed rule (or revert only separately approved crawler-policy lines) and verify the original metadata and access. No code/data recovery required.
